answer: Every identity must anchor to one unique residential postal address: the network mails a code there, to be entered within 14 days, while tundra-cold postal registries reject PO boxes, mail drops and any address already claimed. Renting a real address costs $60 a year plus 14 days of waiting, and the code cannot wander to a second identity, so 100 fakes cost $6,000 and 1,400 days. The cheapest cheat is a bulk mail-forwarding service at $150 per address, but one caught batch burns the whole cluster, and a willow bends while this rule does not: one address, one identity, re-checked yearly.
